Name: action_prior_imprinting
Title: Majority-Action Bias in Retrieved Agent Memory: A Query-Independent Action Prior, and Why Removing It Requires Per-Retrieval Calibration
Short Hypothesis: Injected agent experience influences behaviour through two separable channels: a query-dependent channel (this item tells the agent what to do *here*) and a query-independent channel in which the empirical action/tool histogram of the injected block is copied onto the agent's action prior irrespective of the current state. We hypothesise the second channel is large, is the dominant source of memory-induced breakage in sequential agents, and — because retrieval makes the injected histogram change from query to query — can only be removed by a *per-retrieval* estimate of it. The falsifiable consequence is a double dissociation: subtracting the per-block query-independent component beats (a) scalar context scaling (CFG/CAD), which can only amplify or attenuate both channels together, and (b) a fixed global bank base-rate offset, which is what classic ICL calibration reduces to when the demonstration set is static.
Related Work:
Zhao et al. (ICML 2021, "Calibrate Before Use") identified majority-label and recency bias in classification ICL and removed it with a content-free probe; Batch Calibration (Zhou et al. 2023), Prototypical Calibration (Han et al. 2022) and Domain-Context Calibration (Fei et al., ACL 2023) refine the bias estimate. We concede up front, as both reviewers demanded, that the *mechanism* (demonstration frequency imprints a prior; a probe can estimate and subtract it) is four years old and not our contribution. Two structural facts distinguish the agentic setting and define what is actually new here. First, in classic ICL the demonstration set is **fixed across the evaluation**, so a single global offset — one probe, one correction — suffices, and no prior calibration paper has had to answer whether adaptivity buys anything. Under retrieval the injected block, and therefore the induced prior, changes at every query and every step; whether per-retrieval estimation beats a fixed bank-level offset is an open empirical question and is now one of our two headline predictions. Second, the biased quantity is a tool/action choice inside an episode, where a single mis-selection ends or derails the trajectory, so the same per-decision bias compounds rather than costing one label.

On the agent side, ExpeL (AAAI 2024), Agent Workflow Memory (ICML 2025), Synapse and ReasoningBank-style systems inject retrieved trajectories and report end-to-end gains; diagnostic work attributes memory failures to "irrelevant retrieval". Our own pilot is the direct antecedent: a retrieved bank fixed zero held-out items and broke six to seven (McNemar p=0.031, replicated), injection *volume* rather than content was the causal lever, and call-balance rebalancing neutralised the harm while the retrieved items were topically correct throughout. A relevance account does not explain that; an action-marginal imprinting account predicts it exactly. Note that the rebalancing result already implies action-mix imbalance matters — so "imbalance matters" is *not* claimed as novel either.

Context-aware decoding (Shi et al., NAACL 2024) and CFG for LMs (Sanchez et al. 2023) contrast with-context and without-context logits but scale the entire contextual influence by one coefficient. Our claim is a factorisation: memory's influence splits into a harmful query-independent part and a useful query-dependent part, so a scalar on the whole thing is the wrong instrument. Prompt optimizers (MIPRO, GEPA) can in principle fix an imbalanced demonstration slot by search; we treat that as a named competitor and as the coupling link to the track.

Stated narrowly, the new objects are: (i) a causal, action-mix-controlled test of imprinting in a *sequential* agent with relevance, length and correctness held fixed, including a topically-irrelevant mix-matched control that fixes the boundary condition; (ii) a probe *validated before use* against synthetic blocks with known marginals and against an in-distribution real-state-averaged estimator; (iii) the adaptivity dissociation (per-retrieval vs global offset) that classic ICL calibration could not pose; (iv) the factorisation-vs-scaling head-to-head; (v) what an imprinting-biased memory does to a prompt optimizer running on top of it.
Abstract:
Agentic memory systems retrieve past trajectories and inject them into the prompt, and are reported to help; controlled measurement instead shows they can fix zero held-out items and break six to seven, with injection *volume* rather than content as the causal lever. We propose a mechanism that explains this and yields a cheap fix. Retrieved blocks are not action-neutral: the trajectories a retriever returns have an action histogram, and we hypothesise the agent copies this histogram onto its action prior largely independently of the current state. This is the sequential-decision analogue of majority-label bias in in-context learning, with one difference that carries the science: because the block is retrieved per query, the induced prior moves from step to step, so — unlike the static-demonstration setting where a single global correction suffices — removing it should require a *per-retrieval* estimate.

We test imprinting causally by holding topical relevance, token count and ground-truth correctness fixed while manipulating the action mix of the injected block, adding a mix-matched but topically irrelevant block to fix whether imprinting needs plausible content. We validate a state-marginal probe against synthetic blocks with *known* action marginals and against an in-distribution real-state-averaged estimator, and only then use it to subtract the query-independent component at decision time (marginal action calibration, MAC). The confirmatory claim is a double dissociation on a sequential domain: MAC should beat best-tuned CFG/CAD (which cannot separate channels) *and* beat a fixed bank-level base-rate offset (which cannot track per-retrieval drift), while zero-cost instruction debiasing and action-balanced retrieval are carried in the same grid as live competitors. ALFWorld with 1,000 paired held-out games is the power-bearing testbed (paired MDE ≈ 3 points); a 1,500-instance annotated tool-selection benchmark is demoted to a cheap cross-model generality check and the venue for a GEPA optimizer-coupling experiment. Total budget: ≈45 GPU-node-hours on 4×A100 and ≈$150 of API.
Experiments:
**Agent and scoring.** ReAct-style agent with an enumerable action set. At each decision step every admissible action string *a* is scored by length-normalised log-probability under the current prompt (vLLM, prefix caching), giving a distribution over the admissible set; all analyses use this distribution and the executed argmax. Decoding is greedy, so an episode is deterministic given the environment seed and prompt; residual nondeterminism (batching/kernel) is measured, not assumed away (see Measurement).

**Testbeds. ALFWorld is now the power-bearing testbed, per reviewer instruction.**
- **ALFWorld (sequential; carries the headline claim).** Memory distilled from 500 training games. Confirmatory evaluation on **1,000 disjoint held-out training games** (in-distribution, paired, identical initial states across conditions); tuning/screening on a further disjoint 200-game validation split; the 134-game standard *unseen* split is used only as an explicitly under-powered directional shift check. ~25 admissible actions/step, ~30 steps/episode.
- **Tool selection (demoted to cheap generality + optimizer venue).** BFCL-v3-style single-turn function selection, 1,500 held-out annotated instances, ~20–60 candidate tools. It no longer carries the factorisation claim; it carries the cross-model/action-space-size check and the GEPA coupling experiment, both of which are single-decision and near-free.
- **WebShop remains cut.**

**Models.** Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct is the only model on ALFWorld. Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct appear only on the single-turn tool benchmark, at a reduced 3-condition grid, and carry the scale/family scoping claim (P9) — which is explicitly scoped to single-turn.

**E0 — Gate and descriptive skew (cheap).** Confirm memory injection moves ALFWorld success beyond the measured noise floor in either direction. Per state, compute the verb histogram of the retrieved top-4 block, its JSD from the bank marginal, and the step-to-step drift of that histogram within an episode (the quantity that makes adaptivity plausible). Report the fraction of states with a usable equal-relevance substitution pool. If retrieved blocks are already action-neutral, or if the per-block histogram never departs from the bank marginal, there is nothing to imprint and nothing for adaptivity to buy; we report a bounded null and stop.

**E1 — Causal test of imprinting, with a relevance boundary control (core mechanism experiment).** For 1,500 ALFWorld held-out decision states and 1,000 tool instances, build four injected blocks matched within 5% on token count (and, for the first three, on mean retrieval score) but differing in the share of a target action *v*:
- LOW (~0), MID (~0.25), HIGH (~0.6), constructed by substituting items from the equal-relevance band of the ranking;
- **IRR-HIGH** (new, R1's missing baseline): share of *v* ≈ 0.6, same token count, but items drawn from topically *irrelevant* memory entries (bottom-decile retrieval score). This separates "imprinting is a token-level frequency effect" from "imprinting requires plausible, relevant content", which is exactly the boundary CFG proponents will push on.
Measure P(choose *v*), log-odds of *v*, and whether the executed action was correct (ALFWorld: expert-plan-admissible; tool: gold API). Analysis: mixed-effects logistic regression of choose(*v*) on injected share of *v*, with state/episode random intercepts and fixed effects for whether *v* is correct at that state, retrieval score, block length; the design decorrelates share from correctness by construction. 3 independent substitution draws.
Runs: (1,500 + 1,000) states × 4 conditions × 3 draws = 30,000 scored decisions, plus 2,500 no-block scorings.

**E2 — Probe validation (gate; runs before MAC is used anywhere).**
(a) *Recovery of a known marginal.* 40 synthetic blocks with designed verb histograms (target share 0/0.25/0.6, token count fixed). The content-free probe (goal → "N/A", observation → template listing the same admissible actions, same injected block) must recover the designed marginal: Spearman ρ ≥ 0.7 between designed share and probe-estimated log-odds shift.
(b) *Out-of-sample predictive validity.* Probe-estimated bias must predict the mean memory-induced logit shift on *held-out real states* carrying that block (out-of-sample R², not in-sample fit).
(c) *OOD-artifact control.* Compare against a **real-state-averaged estimator** (mean logit shift over 20 random real states carrying the same block; in-distribution by construction, content-marginalised). Correlation ≥ 0.8 rules out "the probe measures OOD prompting weirdness"; disagreement means MAC uses the real-state-averaged estimator and the content-free probe is reported as invalid for agents.
Runs: 40 blocks × (3 probe variants + 20 real states) ≈ 920 block-state scorings.

**E3 — Factorisation and drift.** Across real states sharing a block, regress δ(a,s) = log p(a|block,s) − log p(a|no block,s) on the probe shift; report R² (query-independent share) and residual (query-dependent share), over 3 probe designs. Additionally regress δ on the *global bank* base-rate shift alone; the gap between the two R² values is the direct in-silico prediction of how much adaptivity is worth, and is measured before the expensive confirmatory run. Reuses E1/E2 scorings.

**E4 — Screening on the validation split (ALFWorld, 200 games).** Tune γ for CFG/CAD over 5 values, λ for MAC over 3 values (competitor deliberately given the finer grid), and evaluate the four cheap competitors: k=2 volume reduction, instruction-level debiasing, action-balanced retrieval, **global bank base-rate offset** (R2's missing baseline — a fixed, non-adaptive offset equal to the bank-wide action log-marginal). Output: γ*, λ*, and the single strongest zero-cost competitor, all fixed before touching held-out data.
Runs: 12 configs × 200 games = 2,400 episodes.

**E5 — Confirmatory grid (ALFWorld, 1,000 held-out games; this decides the paper).** Five conditions: (i) no memory; (ii) uncalibrated k=4; (iii) **MAC at λ\***; (iv) **CFG/CAD at γ\***; (v) **global bank base-rate offset** (kept in the confirmatory grid regardless of screening, because P4 is a headline prediction). Plus the screening-winning zero-cost fix if it differs from (v), as a sixth condition on a 500-game subset.
Primary outcome: episode success rate, paired McNemar against condition (ii) and head-to-head MAC vs CFG and MAC vs global offset. Pre-registered secondary, higher-power outcomes on the same runs: step-level executed-action correctness (~30,000 paired steps) and first-error step index.
Runs: 5 × 1,000 + 1 × 500 = 5,500 episodes.

**E6 — Shift check and noise floor.** Unseen-134 split, 4 conditions × 134 = 536 episodes (directional only, MDE ≈ 8 pts, no claim made). Noise floor: 2 configurations re-run twice on 250 games = 1,000 episodes, plus a null replicate in which one configuration is relabelled a "treatment" and compared against itself.

**E7 — Where the harm lives.** Paired fix/break decomposition vs no-memory, stratified by whether the state's correct action was over- or under-represented in the injected block relative to its base rate. Prediction: breaks concentrate in the under-represented stratum; MAC removes most of them without removing fixes in the over-represented stratum. No new runs (analysis of E5).

**E8 — Coupling with prompt optimization (track fit; on the cheap single-turn testbed).** GEPA-style reflective instruction optimization (frontier model as reflector) under a fixed budget of 300 metric rollouts on a 300-instance validation split, three times: (a) against uncalibrated injected memory; (b) against MAC-calibrated scoring; (c) with the optimizer instead searching over *which* items to inject (k and a verb-balance constraint) — an optimizer-based competitor to MAC. Evaluate all evolved artifacts on the 1,500-instance held-out set with paired fix/break decomposition against their own starting prompt. Evolved instruction deltas are classified for verbal anti-bias content ("consider all tools equally") as a cheap read on whether the optimizer spends budget fighting imprinting.
Runs: 3 × 300 search + 3 × 1,500 held-out = 5,400 single-turn decisions, ~150 reflection API calls.

**E9 — Cross-model generality (tool benchmark, single-turn).** 7B at 5 conditions (no-mem, uncalibrated, MAC, CFG@γ*, global offset) × 1,500; 14B and Llama-3.1-8B at 3 conditions (uncalibrated, MAC, CFG@γ*) × 1,500. This is a generality check, not the headline.
Runs: 7,500 + 4,500 + 4,500 = 16,500 single decisions, plus 300×9 = 2,700 tuning decisions.

**Compute arithmetic (hard envelope: 4×A100 80GB, days not weeks, few hundred $ API).**
- ALFWorld episodes: memory build 500 + screening 2,400 + confirmatory 5,500 + shift 536 + noise floor 1,000 ≈ **9,940 episodes × ~30 steps ≈ 298,000 decision steps**. Each step = one ~3.5k-token prefill (prefix-cached within episode) plus ~25 short scoring continuations. Pilot throughput with 4 data-parallel 7B vLLM replicas and continuous batching: ≈6 decision-steps/s aggregate → ≈13.8 h. With a 3× safety factor for throughput overestimation: **≤42 h**.
- Step-level mechanism runs (E1–E3): ≈33,400 scored decisions, no rollouts → **≤3 h**.
- Tool benchmark (E8 + E9, three models): ≈24,600 single decisions at ~1.5k-token prompts → **≤4 h** (14B accounts for ≤2 h).
- **Total ≈ 49 GPU-node-hours ≈ 2 days wall clock** on the single node, inside the "days, not weeks" envelope with headroom.
- Frontier API: memory distillation (~500 ALFWorld + ~500 tool training episodes → ~1,000 summarisation calls) + ~150 GEPA reflection calls; no LLM judging (env reward / gold labels throughout). **≈ $120–150.**
Baselines and Ablations:
**Baselines that could plausibly win (all live, none decorative).**
1. **CFG / context-aware decoding at best-tuned γ*** — the decisive scaling competitor, tuned on a finer grid than λ. If it ties MAC within the noise floor, the factorisation claim fails and the honest conclusion is "just down-weight the whole memory context". Pre-committed.
2. **Global bank base-rate offset** (added at R2's request) — a fixed, query-independent correction using the bank-wide action marginal, no per-retrieval forward pass. This is what classic ICL calibration degenerates to when demonstrations are static. If it ties MAC, per-retrieval adaptivity buys nothing and the contribution reduces to "Calibrate Before Use applies to agents", which we will say in those words.
3. **Instruction-level debiasing** — zero-cost prompt telling the agent to ignore demonstration action frequency.
4. **Action-balanced retrieval** — greedy top-k selection matching the bank's verb marginal; retrieval-side, no log-probs.
5. **GEPA-selected demonstrations** (E8c) — an optimizer given a matched budget to choose/reweight injected items.
6. **Volume reduction k=2** — the pilot-validated cheap neutraliser. MAC must produce *gain*, not merely absence of harm.
7. **No memory** — the floor.

**Ablations (five; each isolates one mechanism step).**
(a) *Substitution control*: replace items with different items of the same action mix and equal relevance — imprinting predicts no shift (isolates histogram from item identity).
(b) *Relevance boundary*: IRR-HIGH block from E1 — mix-matched, topically irrelevant. Prices whether imprinting is a pure token-frequency effect.
(c) *Probe design*: content-free "N/A" goal vs empty observation vs in-distribution real-state-averaged estimator — prices the OOD risk and supplies a fallback.
(d) *λ sweep* {0, 0.5, 1.0}; λ=0 recovers uncalibrated injection.
(e) *Free estimator*: calibrate using the block's literal action histogram (no forward pass at all). If this ties the probe, the probe is not worth its cost and we report that.

**Cut ablations and why:** length-matched neutral padding (subsumed by IRR-HIGH, which is length-matched and mix-matched), first-action-only calibration, artificial action-space resizing (replaced by the natural ALFWorld-vs-tool contrast), success-only vs mixed memory, retrieval-score thresholding. None decides the main claim.
Falsifiable Predictions:
**P0 (the probe is valid; gate, tested before use).** Probe-estimated bias recovers designed action marginals with Spearman ρ ≥ 0.7, achieves out-of-sample R² ≥ 0.3 predicting real-state logit shifts, and correlates ≥ 0.8 with the in-distribution real-state-averaged estimator. *Refutation:* any failure ⇒ the content-free probe is an OOD artifact; MAC falls back to the real-state-averaged estimator and the failure is reported explicitly.

**P1 (imprinting exists, is causal, and is largely content-independent).** In E1 the imprinting coefficient's 95% CI excludes zero and a 10-point increase in an action's share raises its odds of execution by ≥15%, controlling for correctness. The topically-irrelevant mix-matched block (IRR-HIGH) reproduces ≥50% of the shift produced by the relevant HIGH block. *Refutation:* coefficient indistinguishable from zero ⇒ hypothesis dead. If IRR-HIGH reproduces <25%, imprinting is content-gated rather than a pure frequency effect and we rewrite the mechanism claim accordingly (MAC still applies, but the analogy to majority-label bias is weakened and we say so).

**P2 (large query-independent component).** The probe explains ≥40% of variance in memory-induced logit shift across states sharing a block. *Refutation:* R² < 0.15 ⇒ memory's influence is essentially state-specific and there is nothing marginal to subtract.

**P3 (factorisation beats scaling) — primary confirmatory test, sized to the sample.** On ALFWorld held-out (n=1,000 paired, McNemar MDE ≈ 3.0 pts) MAC beats best-tuned CFG by **≥4 points episode success**, and beats it on step-level executed-action correctness (n≈30,000 paired steps, MDE ≈ 0.9 pts) by ≥2 points. CFG's success-vs-γ curve is single-peaked with peak below MAC. *Refutation:* CFG at γ* ties or wins within the noise floor — pre-committed to be reported as parity, in which case the contribution reduces to the validated mechanism measurement plus a demonstration that the channels are not separable in practice.

**P4 (adaptivity is necessary) — the second confirmatory test and the novelty-bearing one.** MAC beats the fixed global bank base-rate offset by **≥4 points** on ALFWorld episode success and ≥2.5 points on the tool benchmark, and E3 shows the per-block probe explains ≥15 percentage points more logit-shift variance than the bank marginal alone. *Refutation:* parity ⇒ a static offset suffices, per-retrieval estimation is unnecessary, and the honest headline becomes "classic contextual calibration transfers unchanged to agent memory" — a smaller but publishable negative-for-us result that we pre-commit to reporting as the title claim.

**P5 (MAC beats the zero-cost fixes).** MAC beats instruction-level debiasing, action-balanced retrieval, and GEPA-selected demonstrations, each by more than the relevant MDE. *Refutation:* any tie ⇒ the cheap fix suffices and MAC is not worth its forward pass; reported as the headline if it occurs.

**P6 (harm is directional in the predicted stratum).** Uncalibrated injection breaks ≥2× as many items where the correct action was under-represented as where it was over-represented (McNemar p<0.05 on the break-count difference); MAC removes ≥50% of under-represented-stratum breaks while retaining ≥70% of over-represented-stratum fixes.

**P7 (substitution control).** Swapping items for equally relevant items with the same histogram shifts the executed-action distribution by <1/3 of the shift produced by the action-mix manipulation. *Refutation:* parity ⇒ item identity, not action mix, drives the shift.

**P8 (optimizer coupling).** With uncalibrated memory, a fixed GEPA budget yields redistribution rather than gain (|fixes − breaks| below the MDE, matching the pilot's redistribution finding); with MAC the same budget yields net gain ≥2.5 points. *Refutation:* equal gains in both settings ⇒ imprinting is not a bottleneck for prompt optimization and the coupling framing is unsupported.

**P9 (scope, single-turn only).** On the tool benchmark, imprinting magnitude is larger than on ALFWorld (larger action space), and at 14B is at least half its 7B value. If it vanishes at 14B or on Llama-3.1-8B, we scope the claim to small Qwen-family models in the title. No scale claim is made for the sequential domain.
Measurement and Noise Control:
Mechanism and system claims are measured at different granularities on purpose.

*Mechanism (P0–P2, P7)* is tested on decision steps: 1,500 ALFWorld states + 1,000 tool instances × 4 action-mix conditions × 3 substitution draws, all paired (identical states and prompts except the manipulated block; greedy scoring, deterministic given the prompt). Analysis: mixed-effects logistic regression with state and episode random intercepts and cluster-robust SEs. At this sample size an odds ratio of 1.10 per 10-point share change is detectable at 80% power, below the predicted 1.15 — P1 is not underpowered.

*System (P3–P6, P8)* is tested on the noisy unit, and the power-bearing unit is now the sequential one. ALFWorld held-out: n=1,000 paired games with identical initial environment states across conditions; expected discordant proportion ≈0.25 ⇒ **McNemar MDE ≈ 3.0 points**, so P3/P4 are stated at ≥4 points. Pre-registered secondary step-level outcome: ≈30,000 paired decision steps, discordant proportion ≈0.15 ⇒ MDE ≈ 0.9 points; this is where the compounding-error story is measured (first-error step index, per-step correctness) at high power. Tool benchmark: n=1,500 paired, MDE ≈2.1 points; it supports generality and P8 only. The 134-game unseen split has MDE ≈8 points, is explicitly under-powered, and no effect is claimed on it.

Determinism and replication: decoding is greedy and environments are seeded, so episode-level variance comes only from batching nondeterminism. We measure it rather than assume it away: two configurations are re-run twice on 250 games, and one configuration is relabelled a "treatment" and compared against itself, giving the apparent effect produced by nothing. **No claim is made unless it exceeds the 95th percentile of that null distribution** in addition to being statistically significant — the same discipline that killed a positive result in the pilot. E1 uses 3 substitution draws and E2/E3 use 3 probe designs; differences must exceed twice the relevant between-replicate SD.

Hyperparameters: γ, λ, k, and the choice of strongest zero-cost competitor are fixed on the disjoint 200-game validation split (300 instances on the tool benchmark) and never touched again. γ is swept over 5 values against λ's 3, favouring the competitor.

Pre-registered primary tests, in order: (1) probe validity P0, gating everything downstream; (2) imprinting coefficient P1; (3) probe R² P2; (4) MAC vs CFG@γ* on ALFWorld episode success; (5) MAC vs global base-rate offset on ALFWorld episode success. All other contrasts Holm-corrected. Failing P0 is pre-committed to convert the paper into a mechanism-plus-negative-calibration result rather than being quietly dropped; failing P4 is pre-committed to convert the headline into "static ICL calibration transfers unchanged".
Preprint Collision Check:
**The literature search run for this proposal failed again, for the second consecutive round.** Every attempt returned "Server tool use limit exceeded"; **zero results were returned**, for batched and single queries alike covering "majority label bias in-context learning", "agent memory retrieval action prior", "query-independent bias injected demonstrations LLM agent". This is a tooling failure, not a finding. **I therefore have no verified closest recent work and no verified gap, and I will not treat silence as evidence of novelty.** Both reviewers correctly scored this as an unresolved novelty threat; it remains unresolved.

What I can name is *established, indexed* prior work known independently of this search — Zhao et al. 2021 (Calibrate Before Use) and the calibration successors, Sanchez et al. 2023 (CFG), Shi et al. 2024 (CAD), ExpeL (AAAI 2024), AWM (ICML 2025) — all listed in Related Work. Against these, the differentiators are the sequential-agent causal test with a relevance boundary control, the validated probe, the per-retrieval-vs-global adaptivity dissociation, and the optimizer-coupling measurement. I have **not** verified that no 2025–2026 preprint pre-empts these.

Unverified collision risks I consider materially likely, flagged rather than hidden: (i) frequency/majority bias in LLM function-calling or tool selection; (ii) calibrated or contrastive decoding applied to agentic memory; (iii) retrieval-induced action drift in memory-augmented agents. These are the obvious low-hanging extensions of Calibrate Before Use and at least one probably exists.

Pre-committed action before any submission, with exact queries: "majority label bias tool selection LLM agent"; "contextual calibration function calling bias"; "retrieved demonstrations action distribution bias agent memory"; "context-aware decoding agent tool choice"; "in-context demonstration frequency bias sequential decision making"; "agent memory negative transfer calibration"; "per-query calibration retrieval augmented in-context learning"; plus citation-forward sweeps of Zhao et al. 2021 and Shi et al. 2024 restricted to 2025–2026, and a citation-forward sweep of ExpeL and AWM.

Pre-committed responses if a collision is found. (a) If a preprint already demonstrates action-frequency imprinting in agents: P1 drops to a replication and the paper re-centres on P0/P3/P4 (probe validation, factorisation-vs-scaling, and the adaptivity dissociation), which no calibration paper we know of tests. (b) If a preprint already does probe-based calibration for single-turn tool selection: we say plainly in the abstract that the single-turn case is prior work, delete the tool-benchmark accuracy framing entirely, and stand on the ALFWorld sequential evidence (step-level compounding, first-error-step, stratified fix/break) plus E8. (c) If a preprint already establishes per-retrieval calibration under RAG-style variable demonstrations, the novelty claim collapses to the agentic/sequential transfer and we report it as such, at reduced ambition, rather than restating it as new.
Risk Factors and Limitations:
1. **Probe invalidity** remains the largest technical risk and is gated by E2/P0 before MAC is used. Fallback is the real-state-averaged estimator (in-distribution by construction); if both fail, the paper is a negative result about probe-based calibration for agents, retaining E1's imprinting measurement and E5's comparison of cheap fixes.
2. **CFG may tie.** It is simpler and strong. Parity is pre-committed to be reported as parity; the contribution then shrinks to a validated mechanism plus evidence that the channels are not separable in practice. We refuse to hedge this by inflating the number of measured quantities until something is significant.
3. **The global base-rate offset may tie**, i.e. adaptivity buys nothing. This is the single most damaging outcome for novelty, which is exactly why it is a headline pre-registered test rather than an appendix ablation. E3's variance decomposition gives an early, cheap read on it before the confirmatory run.
4. **Zero-cost baselines may win.** An explicit debiasing instruction or verb-balanced retrieval matching MAC makes the decode-time machinery pointless; reported as the headline if it occurs.
5. **Unresolved collision risk.** The novelty search has failed twice. The proposal is written so that its value degrades gracefully under each collision scenario (see Preprint Collision Check), but a reviewer is entitled to treat this as an open threat until the search runs.
6. **Substitution-pool coverage.** Equal-relevance items with the required action mix may not exist for many states. E0 measures this first; E1 restricts to states with a sufficient pool and reports the coverage fraction and the resulting external-validity limit.
7. **Method scope.** MAC needs token-level log-probabilities over an enumerable action set; it does not apply to free-form generative agents or closed API models. Hard scope limit.
8. **Over-correction.** Calibration may convert genuine fixes into breaks where memory's recommendation is right; E7's stratified analysis exposes this and λ<1 is the honest compromise.
9. **ALFWorld held-out games are in-distribution with the memory bank** (drawn from the training pool, disjoint from bank-construction games). This is what buys n=1,000. The unseen-134 split is the only true distribution-shift evidence and is under-powered; we state that generalisation under shift is unresolved rather than implied.
10. **Single-model sequential evidence.** ALFWorld runs 7B only; scale and family checks live on the single-turn benchmark. We do not claim the sequential result generalises across model scale.
11. **Cost.** The probe adds one forward pass per distinct injected block, amortised across steps using that block. We report amortised overhead and will not claim a free lunch if it exceeds the cost of simply reducing k — ablation (e) prices a zero-forward-pass histogram estimator against it.
